content:
Early voting in Texas ended October 30 at 8 p.m., with Webb County turnout running nearly 30% above the pace of the last midterm election, according to KGNS.

The early-voting period opened strong: more than 5,000 ballots were cast on the first day, and the count reached nearly 14,000 by Day 3, according to the report. More than 3,600 voters cast ballots on October 29 alone. The busiest site, the Laredo Fire Department Administration Building, averaged about 1,100 people per day in the first week and about 900 per day in the second week.

Webb County Elections Administrator Jose Luis Castillo said he had expected higher turnout because of interest in several races, but not turnout at a presidential-election level — and that is essentially what occurred, according to KGNS.

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, with 38 countywide polling locations. Voters may vote at any designated location regardless of their home precinct, may ask workers to direct them elsewhere if lines are long, and may not use cellphones inside polling sites. Voters are advised to review the races in advance or bring a paper sample ballot.

Sources:

  • KGNS, "Webb County early voting climbs nearly 30% above 2022 midterm pace," October 30, 2026
